title: Coefficient square for refinement with dense source and arbitrary target
statement: Fix a prime ell and a field k of positive characteristic different from ell. Let X and Y be separated finite-type k-schemes, f:X to Y a k-morphism, and a:Lambda to Lambda-prime a listed coefficient map. Let c be a compactification with quasi-compact open, d a scheme-theoretically dense compactification of f with quasi-compact open, and r:d to c a boundary-preserving refinement. For K in Dctf(X,Lambda), write C_c and C_d for the specified sfbScalarCompactComparison maps, and rho_r for compactificationRefinementComponent. Then T_Y(rho_r(K)) followed by C_d(K) equals C_c(K) followed by rho_r(T_X K). This is a morphism equality in the ordinary unbounded derived category of internal Lambda-prime modules. The target c need not be dense.

source.place: Independence: comparison with refinements; parent DAG steps 3--4, normalization through the schematic closure

proof.text: The ambient scheme of c is Noetherian, being proper over a finite-type k-scheme. Normalize c to the schematic closure c0 of X using the quasi-compact scheme-theoretic image. Its open is c.i.toImage, its closed inclusion into c.Z is c.i.imageι, and its proper map is that inclusion followed by c.g. The normalization has the canonical unbounded derived identification.

source.place: Independence: comparison with refinements; parent DAG steps 3--4, normalization through the schematic closure

proof.text: Let r:d to c have dense source. Since precomposition with d.i does not change the kernel ideal of r and d.i followed by r is c.i, the kernels of r and c.i agree. The closed-immersion universal property factors r through c0. Cancel c.i.imageι to verify both triangles. Dense-source rigidity and the proper/open section lemma identify the inverse image of X with X, so this factor is a boundary-preserving refinement between dense models. The closure inclusion also preserves the open by the image factorization pullback square.

source.place: Independence: comparison with refinements; parent DAG steps 3--4, normalization through the schematic closure

proof.text: Apply scalarRefinementClosureSquare to the factor between dense models and to the closure inclusion. Its final clause gives the two pushed coefficient squares. Their maps scalarRefinementPushforward equal compactificationRefinementComponent: the canonical right-derived compositor is the conjugate of the canonical derived pullback compositor, and deriving a congruence is equality transport, checked by equality induction.

source.place: Independence: comparison with refinements; parent DAG steps 3--4, normalization through the schematic closure

proof.text: The two geometric refinements compose to r by cancellation of the closed inclusion. Transitivity of refinement components over both coefficient rings and functoriality of scalar change paste the two squares. Reassociate and substitute their composite components to obtain precisely the displayed dense-source refinement square. This uses no invertibility to paste the squares.

lean.statement:
theorem scalarDenseRefinementSquare
    (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k]
    [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ell)]
    {Λ Λ' : ScalarSixRing.{u}} (a : Λ ⟶ Λ') (_ha : ListedCoefficientMap ell a)
    {X Y : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] [IsSeparated X.hom]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom] [IsSeparated Y.hom]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (c : Compactification.BoundaryCompactification f.left)
    (d : Compactification.DenseBoundaryCompactification f.left) (r : d.obj ⟶ c)
    (K : ConstantModelConstructibleFiniteTor Λ.X X.left) :
    (scalarSixChange a Y.left).map (compactificationRefinementComponent Λ.X r K.obj) ≫
        sfbScalarCompactComparison a d.obj.obj.obj.i d.obj.obj.obj.g K.obj =
      sfbScalarCompactComparison a c.obj.obj.i c.obj.obj.g K.obj ≫
        compactificationRefinementComponent Λ'.X r
          ((scalarSixChange a X.left).obj K.obj)
